confirmed.problem: Choosing every other project row announces `"<Project name>. Tasks, Timeline and Planning all moved with it."` Choosing "All projects" announces `"the project. Tasks, Timeline and Planning all moved with it."` The line is `var name = (P.list.find(p => p.id === id) || {}).name || "the project";` — `P.ALL` is not a member of `P.list`, so the internal fallback literal falls straight into the live region. Confirmed by driving: `#say` reads exactly "the project. Tasks, Timeline and Planning all moved with it." while the head correctly repaints to "All projects · 10 of 40 done · 3 projects, day 11 of 356".
confirmed.consequence: The one switch that changes the most — from a single wedding to everything Orla is running at once — is the one the product cannot name aloud. A screen-reader user hears a sentence that begins mid-phrase and identifies nothing, so the largest context change in the application is the least legible one. It is also the studio's private placeholder text arriving in the accessibility tree, a class this library has already paid for three times.
confirmed.fix: Resolve the name before the fallback: `var row = P.list.find(function (p) { return p.id === id; }); var name = id === P.ALL ? "All projects" : (row ? row.name : null);` and if `name` is still null, say nothing rather than say a placeholder.
confirmed.assertion: At 1440x960, open `.projMenu` and activate `.projItem[data-project="all"]`: assert `#say` begins with "All projects." and contains no occurrence of the string "the project.".
confirmed.verdict: CONFIRMED — every claim reproduces verbatim, the code reads exactly as quoted, and no gate covers it. DRIVEN (chromium, 1440x960, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`), reading `#say` after each switch: - `.projItem[data-project="academic"]` → `"Academic Year 2026. Tasks, Timeline and Planning all moved with it."` - `.projItem[data-project="school"]` → `"Secondary School Year 2026. Tasks, Timeline and Planning all moved with it."` - `.projItem[data-project="all"]` → `"the project. Tasks, Timeline and Planning all moved with it."` MECHANISM, verified in source. `src/tasks.js:2658` is `const name = (P.list.find((p) => p.id === id) || {}).name || "the project";`. `src/projects.js:465-477` exposes `list` as a getter over `var PROJECTS = [ORCHARD, ACADEMIC, SCHOOL]` (line 272) and `ALL: ALL_ID` where `ALL_ID = "all"` (line 339) — a sibling key, never a member of the array. `apply()` branches on the same id (`id === ALL_ID ? applyAll() : applyProject(id)`), so the switch itself is correct; only the sentence falls through to the developer literal. Four of five rows in the menu name themselves; one speaks the fallback. Not restating a gate: I grepped `interaction-check.mjs` for `moved with it`, `projItem`, `data-project` and `All projects` — zero hits. The behaviour gate asserts nothing about the project switcher, so this is genuinely past what automation sees. It is also not a re-file: no closed or refuted finding touches the switcher's live region. SEVERITY — the seat left the class implicit; I put it at defect, not misleading or blocking. The switch itself is correct and complete (I confirmed `B.workspace`, the ledger and the switcher label all repaint to "All projects · 3 projects, day 11 of 356"), and focus lands on `[data-act="projects"]` whose `aria-label` reads "All projects, switch project" — so a screen-reader user does hear the right name one utterance later. Nothing is asserted that is untrue; a placeholder is simply audible where a name should be. Audibly wrong, passable, worth fixing at this bar because it is the one row of five that does not say its own name. ON THE PROPOSED FIX — it works, so I am not refuting on it, but it is second-best and I would not ship it as written. It hardcodes a fourth copy of the literal "All projects" inside `tasks.js`, where three already exist and are generated (`allProjects()` sets `board.workspace` and `timeline.project.name`, and `projectMenu()` prints `All projects`). Adding a private copy inside the announcer is precisely the divergence class this surface keeps paying for — the spoken name and the printed name would then be two strings that have to be kept equal by hand. Its second half ("if `name` is still null, say nothing") also prescribes silence after a completed state change; that branch is unreachable from the UI (every `data-act="project"` row is minted from `P.list` or `P.ALL`), so it is dead code that reads like a policy.
confirmed.breaks:
Plausible breakage is small but real, and it is all in the coupling this fix deliberately creates. `B.workspace` becomes load-bearing for speech, so any future change that lets `board.workspace` hold something other than a bare name — a name plus a count, a period, an em-dash suffix — would drag that decoration into the spoken line. If that ever happens, the announcer needs its own name field on the world object, not a longer expression here.

Re-measure after it lands: (1) `#say` after switching to each of the five rows — the three fixtures, `all`, and a project created through `project-new` — and assert each equals `[the switcher's own label] + ". Tasks, Timeline and Planning all moved with it."` rather than a hardcoded expectation, which is the invariant worth gating; (2) the rename path at `src/tasks.js:585` still says "Renamed to X." and the create path still says "X. New project, nothing in it yet." — neither is touched, but both read `B` after the same `mount()`; (3) re-run `interaction-check.mjs`, which currently asserts nothing here — this is the moment to add the assertion in (1), since a switcher with no behaviour coverage is how this survived to round four; (4) `audit.mjs` needs nothing re-measured: no rule, no token, no box changes, and the sentence is spoken, never painted.

refuted.problem: A/B measured at 1440x960 on `tasks.board`, same card, same board. Real pointer travel from To do to Review (mouse down, 30-step move, mouse up) announces: "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company moved to the review column." Keyboard carry — focus card, Space, ArrowRight, Enter — moves the card exactly as advertised (To do 3→2, In progress 3→4, verified by counting `.card` per `.tray`) and announces: "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company. Task open." Two sentences for one action, and the keyboard one drops the destination lane entirely and replaces it with a report that a panel opened. During the carry the lane IS spoken ("In progress, position 1 of 4."), so the fact exists in the model and is discarded at exactly the moment it becomes permanent. This is not `carry-drop-announces-the-wrong-thing` (r1) — that finding was refuted as wrong about the code; this is a direct comparison of the two paths' output strings against each other.
refuted.why:
REFUTED — the finding measured a key that is not the drop key, and the real drop path already says exactly what the finding demands.

DRIVEN, chromium 1440x960, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, MutationObserver on the single `[aria-live="polite"]` region (`.sr`), lane counts read as `.card` per `.tray`.

1. The keyboard drop is Space, not Enter — and the artifact says so in two channels. `src/tasks.js:1005-1009` renders the in-hand strip as `↑↓←→ move · Space drop · Esc cancel`, and `src/tasks.js:365` sets `aria-keyshortcuts="Space ArrowUp ArrowDown ArrowLeft ArrowRight"` on the card. Enter appears in neither. I read that strip live during the carry: "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company / ↑↓←→ move / Space drop / Esc cancel".

2. The real drop path names the lane. Space, ArrowRight, Space, same card, same board: `todo:3→2, doing:3→4`, and the region says **"Confirm marquee sides with the hire company dropped in the in progress column."** (`src/tasks.js:2369`, `say(task.title + " dropped " + inLane(lane) + ".")`, `inLane` at 1492 = `"in the " + laneMid(id) + " column"`). The load-bearing claim — "the keyboard one drops the destination lane entirely and replaces it with a report that a panel opened" — is false about the code and false when driven.

3. What the seat actually measured was Enter mid-carry, which is not a drop and does not make anything permanent. After Space, ArrowRight, Enter I get the quoted "…Task open." — but the carry strip is still on screen reading "Space drop / Esc cancel", `carriedId` is still set (Enter at `src/tasks.js:2379-2394` never clears it), and pressing Escape immediately afterwards restores `todo:3, doing:3` and says "Move cancelled. …is back in the to do column." So the finding's own thesis — that the lane fact "is discarded at exactly the moment it becomes permanent" — is wrong twice over: the fact is not discarded on the drop, and the Enter moment is not permanent. The mid-carry lane counts the seat cites (3→2, 3→4) are the *provisional* live positions `carryMove` maintains, not a landing.

4. This is a re-file of an already-killed finding. The seat pre-empts `carry-drop-announces-the-wrong-thing` (r1), but the behaviour it actually exercised is `enter-during-carry-does-not-drop` (r1), refuted in round 1. No regression is cited and none exists — I confirmed the r1 behaviour still stands as adjudicated.

5. The fix would make the product lie. It proposes emitting `"<title> moved to the <lane> column. Task open."` on "the keyboard drop path" — i.e. on Enter, since the Space path already carries the lane. Enter is the open-the-task key on every route into the panel (click at 2803, keyboard at 2392, pointerup), and on a carried card it opens the panel with the card still in hand. Emitting a completed-move sentence there would assert a move that Escape can still undo — a polite region stating an untruth, which is precisely the class this engagement closed at `timeline-live-region-is-rebuilt…` and `carry-drop-is-not-undoable`. It would also fire "moved to the … column" on every ordinary Enter-to-open of a card that was never carried at all, unless guarded, which the fix does not mention.

Residual worth naming, not confirming: pointer drop says "moved to the review column" (toLane, 3003) while keyboard drop says "dropped in the in progress column" (inLane, 2369) — two verbs and two prepositions for two genuinely different gestures. That is a defensible distinction (a drag moves; a carry is put down), it is not what the finding argued, and the finding's own numbers about it are wrong, so it does not rescue the verdict.

refuted.why:
REFUTED — the census is a static-DOM dump read as a driven census, it misses half its own evidence, and the fix would create the two-grammar split it claims to remove.

WHAT REPRODUCES. Driven, chromium, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=…` at 1440×960 and 390×844, enumerating every `[aria-disabled="true"]` in all eight states. The two quoted strings are verbatim correct and in the right places: `src/tasks.js:799` → `.ghost[aria-label="More"]` `title="Project settings come with your account."`, visible at both widths; `src/tasks.js:536,787` → `.ghost.headSearch` `title="Search comes with the other views."`, `display:none` by default (`src/tasks.css:365`) and `inline-flex` only at ≤720 (`src/tasks.css:1980`), so "visible only at 390" is right. Both targets are indeed shut: the account tile is `aria-disabled` "Your account, in Signal Studio. Not here yet."; List/Schedule/Calendar are `aria-disabled` "Board is the only view for now." All confirmed.

WHY IT FAILS — THE CENSUS IS WRONG, AND WRONG IN THE DIRECTION THAT KILLS THE ARGUMENT. The claim is "two of the seven." Driven rather than dumped, Tasks carries FOUR strings in the deferring grammar, all reachable and all live:
1. "Search comes with the other views." — `.headSearch` (≤720).
2. "Project settings come with your account." — `.ghost[aria-label="More"]`.
3. "Setting a milestone comes with the Schedule view." — `.drawerAdd`, `src/tasks.js:1298`. Reached in two clicks: Planning → Milestones tab. I inventoried it visible, `aria-disabled="true"`, label "Add a milestone".
4. "Choosing a specific day comes with the Schedule view." — `.dayMenu` last `menuitem`, `src/tasks.js:1326`. Reached: Planning → any "Pick a day". Pressing it puts "Choosing a specific day comes with the Schedule view." into the live region.
(3) and (4) defer to Schedule — the same `segItem` that says "Board is the only view for now." That is precisely the defect the finding names, twice over, in the same product, and the finding did not find it. So the deferring grammar is not two strays against five plain sentences; it is a deliberate, four-strong secondary register meaning "this arrives with a named surface", running alongside the plain "Not here yet." register for doors that name no surface. The engagement's own instruction is to grade by driving; a copy-consistency census taken off the initial DOM was always going to miss half of it, and here the missing half reverses the conclusion.

WHY THE FIX MAKES IT WORSE. Rewriting only (1) and (2) leaves (3) and (4) untouched. Tasks would then hold two grammars where it currently holds one consistent one — two "…comes with the Schedule view." strings sitting one drawer away from a magnifier that has just been taught to say "Not here yet." That is the exact class already killed twice at this panel (three-unavailability-grammars r1, closed-doors-two-treatments r3) and it lands on the wrong side of it.

Worse, `title="Searching your tasks. Not here yet."` puts the search door into open self-contradiction. `src/tasks.js:2274` announces `say("Search arrives with the other views.")` on Ctrl/⌘K; I drove it and read exactly that from `[aria-live]` at both 1440 and 390. Today the magnifier's tooltip and the shortcut's announcement agree on the fact and differ only in verb. After the fix, pressing the magnifier says "Not here yet." and pressing Ctrl+K says "Search arrives with the other views." — one door, two incompatible answers, on a surface where that is the named sin.

The fix also deletes information for symmetry. "Project settings come with your account" is the only place in the product that says where project settings will live — which matters, because the rail already carries a *different* settings door ("Your workspace, your way. Not here yet."). Collapsing it to "Project settings. Not here yet." leaves two settings doors saying near-identical nothings and drops the one fact that distinguishes them.

refuted.problem: Ctrl+Z on the Timeline changes the data and says nothing. Press Ctrl+Z: the field returns to "1 August 2026", .b-undoText is emptied to "", and both #say and .b-live are empty strings. On a freshly loaded owner-flight, desk and phone, Ctrl+Z with an empty stack is also completely silent, where Tasks answers "Nothing left to undo." and Notes answers "Taken back. Nothing went to Tasks." Reading the source, undo() restores the record, repaints the bar, restores focus and restores scroll, and never calls window.__SUITE.say.
refuted.why:
REFUTED — the headline is false on the seat's own repro, the cross-product comparison it argues from is false, and two of the three states it names have no undo to be mute about.

1. "Changes the data and says nothing" is wrong. I ran the seat's exact repro (chromium, 1440x960, `?v=paper&state=timeline.owner-flight`, `.b-grab` then `.b-step[data-delta="7"]` then Ctrl+Z) with a MutationObserver on every `[role="status"],[aria-live]` node. On the undo, `.b-stepRead` — `role="status"`, visible, sitting in the editor the operator is standing in, `src/timeline.js:1694` — goes "Saturday 8 August 2026 / in 23 days" → "Saturday 1 August 2026 / in 16 days". `setAway` is the undo closure (`undo: function () { setAway(root, item, from); }`, line 1592) and `setAway` writes `readParts[0]`/`readParts[1]` on the way through, so the restored date and the restored distance are both announced, politely, in the panel the keypress happened in. The seat enumerated `#say`, `.b-live` and `.b-undoText` and missed the one region the editor has for exactly this. Silence is not what the product does here.

2. "Notes answers 'Taken back. Nothing went to Tasks.'" is false. That is Notes' undo-of-a-send sentence (`notes.js:1136,1179`), not its empty-stack answer. `doUndo()` opens `if (!undone) return false;` (`notes.js:308-309`) — no `say`. Driven on `notes.notebook` with focus on a `.railTile`, Ctrl+Z leaves `#say` at `""`; only `tasks.board` answers "Nothing left to undo." So Timeline already matches Notes, and Tasks is the outlier. The finding's premise — Timeline alone against two answering siblings — is 1-of-2, and its fix, scoped to Timeline only, would make Notes the new odd one out rather than closing an inconsistency.

3. Two of the three named states are the guest. `timeline.desk` and `timeline.phone` are the **Received** states (`STATES`, lines 67-68: "Received · phone", "Received · desk"). Measured: `.b-grab` 0, `.b-edit` absent, `.b-step` 0, `.b-undo` 0 in both. The handler exits at `if (!live) return;` because there is no bar. Making those two say "Nothing left to undo." would assert an editing model the recipient of a shared timeline does not have — the fix is worse than the silence on two of its three surfaces.

4. The fix's mechanism does not exist. It says to reuse "the same parts paintUndo writes into `.b-undoText`, turned round". Those parts are the forward sentence: `["Menu tasting at The Orchard moved ", 7, " days ", "later."]`. The exemplar reversal ("is Saturday 1 August, 16 days away") contains a date and a day count that appear nowhere in them; they come from the record after restore. Turned round mechanically, the array yields "Put back. Menu tasting at The Orchard moved 7 days later." — the opposite of what just happened. Five entry kinds (step, rename, visibility, delete, add) each need their own reversal copy; the finding prices this as a one-line addition.

5. What the fix would break: routing the stepper reversal through `__SUITE.say` fires `#say` and `.b-stepRead` on one keypress, two polite regions in the same panel, on the most frequent reversal in the product — the duplicate-announcement class this engagement has already paid to kill once (`the-seam-says-it-twice`, r3).

What survives is thin and refinement-class, not the blocking-shaped thing the write-up implies: `undo()` genuinely never calls `say` (confirmed — the only `__SUITE.say` in `timeline.js` is line 2983, the orientation switch), so the reversals that do not pass through `setAway` — rename, hide/show, delete — get no spoken confirmation beyond the field value or `aria-pressed` changing under the focused control, and the delete case (row reappears, focus elsewhere) is the one genuinely mute path. Nothing is asserted untrue and nothing fails to work, so this is refinement, not defect.

The strip therefore carries the pointer branch's verb for both routes. refuted.why:
REFUTED — the two quoted sentences are verbatim correct, and every claim the finding builds on top of them is false.

DRIVEN, Chromium 1440x960, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, card `demo-t-01` "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company", both routes into `doing`:

- Space / ArrowRight / Space → `#say` reads, in order: "Picked up Confirm marquee sides with the hire company." → "In progress, position 1 of 4." → "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company dropped in the in progress column." `document.querySelector(".carry")` after the drop: **null**.
- Real pointer travel (mouse.down, 20 interpolated moves, mouse.up) → `#say`: "…moved to the in progress column."; `.carry`: "…moved to In progress · Undo · Ctrl Z".

1. **"The strip therefore carries the pointer branch's verb for both routes" is false — the keyboard route has no strip.** The Space drop is `src/tasks.js:2369`, `say(task.title + " dropped " + inLane(lane) + ".")`, and it calls no `arm()`. `arm({kind:"move"…})` exists at exactly two sites — `src/tasks.js:2775` (the card menu's "moveto") and `:2992` (`onDrop`) — and `footPill()` renders the move strip only off `undone`. There is no strip standing over the keyboard drop to be in two vocabularies with, and no "same breath" for the cited rule to govern.

2. **The rule the finding says was not carried over to the move IS carried over to the move.** The strip's move branch (`src/tasks.js:1038`) prints "moved to {Lane}"; both branches that can arm it speak "moved " + `toLane()` = "moved to the {lane} column" (`:2776`, `:3003`). Strip verb and spoken verb agree on every route that produces that strip. The rule at `:1032` is satisfied, not violated.

3. **What actually remains is a verb difference between two different gestures, and the current copy is the better of the two.** The keyboard route is a narrated carry — picked up → position → dropped — and while the card is in hand the foot pill prints, on screen, `Space drop` (`footPill()`, `:1008`; driven text "Space · drop"). "Dropped" is the closing half of "picked up" and the exact word the key legend the operator just read promised. The pointer drag narrates no pick-up; "moved to" is the whole event in one sentence. Two coherent families, each internally consistent (`endCarry` "put down in the {lane} column", Esc "Move cancelled. … is back in the {lane} column" — all `inLane`, all carry-vocabulary). This is taste stated as a defect.

4. **The fix would manufacture the defect the finding invokes.** Make the Space drop say "moved to the in progress column" and the spoken confirmation stops matching the `Space drop` keycap drawn on the sheet at the moment of the press — one act, the legend saying drop and the voice saying moved. It also strands "put down in the {lane} column" as the near-synonym for an abandoned carry against "moved to" for a deliberate one.

5. **The fix's printed half is not this finding's to make.** "all three read … 'moved to {Lane}' printed" requires the carry drop to arm an undo, which it does not; printing the strip without arming would put an Undo button over an act it does not undo (it would pop whatever is beneath in `undoHistory`). Arming it is the remedy of `carry-drop-is-not-undoable` (r3), already adjudicated. And there is no "one sentence builder": the strip uses `laneName()` (title case, no noun), the voice uses `laneMid()` + " column" (`:1474`–`:1500`) — the fix's own target strings keep the two renderings it says it is unifying.

Severity: refinement at most, not the class this seat's framing implies. Nothing is untrue on either route and nothing fails to work; two accurate sentences for two distinct gestures is not the product asserting something false.

REFUTED ON THE FIX ONLY. The problem is real, every measurement is exact, and it must NOT be discarded — but the fix re-opens a copy decision that r1 already adjudicated and rejected, and it leaves live the one instance r1 called the sharpest.

WHAT I CONFIRMED (chromium, 1440x960, ?v=paper&state=notes.seam and =timeline.owner-flight)
Both controls are back, both are pure closes, and the seat's numbers are not approximate — they are the element top-lefts, exactly. L-05 verbatim.

AND IT IS NOT A REGRESSION — IT NEVER LANDED. r1's sharpenedFix was three edits. All three are still unapplied: the peel label, the Timeline label, and `src/notes.js:3211` `say("Done. Your note stayed here.")`. Nothing was fixed and then broken; the record was closed against an assertion nothing enforced. That does not weaken the finding — the product is in the state the seat measured — but it changes what the remedy has to cover.

WHY THE FIX IS REFUTED

1. THE NOTES HALF RE-OPENS AN ADJUDICATED DECISION, ON THE SAME GROUND IT WAS REJECTED. r1 ruled on "Close" for this exact button: "safe but out of register — Notes says 'Put it back', 'Back to your notes', 'Decide later', and the string 'Close' appears nowhere in that product." 2. THE FIX LEAVES THE SHARPEST INSTANCE LIVE, AND CREATES A NEW DISAGREEMENT. `src/notes.js:3211` — the handler for this very button — announces `say("Done. Your note stayed here.")`. Under the seat's fix the button reads "Close" and the screen reader says "Done." A sighted operator is helped; a screen-reader operator still hears "Done" as the first word after dismissing a receipt in a suite where Done is a lane, and now the label and the announcement disagree, which is worse than today's honest consistency. A fix that claims to end the collision must not leave the audio channel saying the word.

3. THE GATE ASSERTION AS WRITTEN WOULD PASS ON BROKEN CODE. I swept all eight resting states at 1440 for any focusable element whose accessible name matches /^Done$/i: zero hits. Both instances exist only after a gesture (Send; `.b-grab`). A static sweep — the obvious reading of "anywhere in the suite" — goes green against the current, unfixed file, which is L-06 failed on its first day. It also must not test the accessible name only: it has to catch the `say()` string.

WHAT IS RIGHT: the Timeline half. "Close" there is correct, is r1's own prescription ("Timeline's register is spatial and unclaimed here"), and keeping `data-act="done"` keeps the `closeEditor` route intact.

SEVERITY: defect, and the seat did not overstate it. The button invites, it does not assert; pressing it closes the peel, the card stays in Tasks, and the 30-second undo is still live. Visibly wrong, passable, cheap. Not misleading.

REFUTED ON THE FIX AND ON ONE LOAD-BEARING CLAUSE — the Escape half of the problem is real, new, and must NOT be discarded.

DRIVEN, chromium, 1440x960, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, first card `demo-t-01`. Every number reproduces: Space → "Picked up Confirm marquee sides with the hire company.", `aria-grabbed="true"`; ArrowRight → tray card counts 3,3,2,0,5 → 2,4,2,0,5 and "In progress, position 1 of 4."; Enter → `.taskPanel` renders, `document.activeElement` is the ASIDE, `carriedId` still set (`aria-grabbed="true"` on the card), live region reads only "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company. Task open."; Escape → counts revert to 3,3,2,0,5, "Move cancelled. … is back in the to do column.", `.taskPanel` still in the DOM, focus on `.card[data-id="demo-t-01"]` at (128, 196.8, 234x135.75), and `document.elementFromPoint` at its centre returns `div.tpScrim`. Second Escape → "Task closed." The seat's repro is exact.

WHAT IS FACTUALLY WRONG. "nothing spoken or drawn says the card is still in the air" is false on the drawn half, and that half is precisely what killed this finding's r1 ancestor (`enter-during-carry-does-not-drop`, refuted: "the HUD still names the drop key"). `footPill()` in `src/tasks.js` renders inside `.sheet` and is unconditional on the panel: with the modal open I measured `.carry` at (496, 826, 529.9x36), computed opacity 1, reading "Confirm marquee sides with the hire company · ↑↓←→ move · Space drop · Esc cancel". `.tpScrim` is `rgba(17,17,17,0.32)` with no backdrop-filter, so the strip is dimmed and fully legible — I clipped a screenshot of it and read every word. The card also still carries `data-force="moving"`. So the surface does keep saying the card is in the air, in the one place it has always said it, and it keeps naming Space and Esc there. Only the spoken sentence omits it — the r1-adjudicated refinement.

That also caps the class. Not blocking and not misleading: the panel prints no Esc keycap at all (`taskPanel()` offers a `.tpClose` button and `data-act="task-close"` on the scrim, no shortcut text), and the only Escape the product advertises anywhere on this screen is the carry strip's "Esc cancel" — which is exactly what Escape does. Nothing the product says fails, and nothing untrue is asserted. It is a defect: focus genuinely leaves an `aria-modal="true"` dialog onto scrimmed content, and a board move silently reverts where the operator cannot see it. It is recoverable — Tab pulls focus back to `.tpClose` via the existing trap, and a second Escape closes the panel — which is why it is not more.

WHY THE FIX IS WRONG. It repeats, verbatim, the second half of the r1 refutation: making Enter commit adds a drop key that neither `aria-keyshortcuts="Space ArrowUp ArrowDown ArrowLeft ArrowRight"` (Enter deliberately absent) nor the carry strip ("Space drop · Esc cancel") names, and the fix names neither. It is worse than a naming gap. Enter's one documented meaning on a card is open-the-note; under this fix, asking to read a card irreversibly commits a move — and if the operator had walked it into Done, fires `completed()` and its receipt — as a side effect of reading. Today Escape restores the pre-carry position; after the fix that recovery path is gone. It also does not repair the real severity in the general case: any other way of opening the panel mid-carry, and the pointer route through `data-act="task-close"`, are untouched.
standing.sharpenedFix: Fix the Escape ladder, not Enter. In `onKey` in `src/tasks.js`, the branch already states its own rule — "Innermost first … an open panel is the innermost thing on the sheet" — and then sites `if (carriedId)` above `if (openTaskId)`, contradicting it. Move the `if (openTaskId)` block above the `if (carriedId)` block, so a live modal owns the first Escape. When it closes with a carry still live, restate the carry rather than dropping it silently: `say("Task closed. " + taskById(carriedId).title + " is still in hand, " + inLane(laneIds()[place(carriedId).x]) + ". Space drops it, Esc cancels.")`, and let `refocus` land on the carried card, not the previously-open one. The second Escape then cancels the move exactly as the strip advertises. Enter, the Space commit path, `completed()`, `aria-keyshortcuts` and the carry strip all stay untouched. Separately, and as a sentence change only with no state change, append the carry clause to the Enter announcement: `say(title + ". Task open. " + title + " is still in hand.")` — that is the one part of the seat's proposal worth keeping, in words instead of in state. Apply the same restatement to the pointer close (`data-act="task-close"` on `.tpScrim` and `.tpClose`) so both routes out of the panel resolve the carry identically.
standing.breaks: The reorder makes cancelling a carry cost two Escapes whenever a panel is open over it, which is correct but is a change to a gesture the strip advertises as one key — re-measure that the strip is still drawn and still reads "Esc cancel" at the moment the second press is expected. Re-measure after it lands: that `refocus` puts focus on the still-carried card and not the just-closed task when the two differ; that the card survives the repaint with `aria-grabbed="true"` and `data-force="moving"` intact (the panel close calls `mount()`, and `mount()` clears `carriedId` on some paths — line 3014 and line 461 both null it, so confirm neither fires here); that `document.elementFromPoint` at the focused card's centre now returns the card, not `div.tpScrim`; that the Tab trap has nothing left to catch, i.e. focus is never outside `.taskPanel` while `.taskPanel` exists; that the pointer route through the scrim and `.tpClose` produces the same sentence and the same focus as Escape; and that the carry strip does not flash the `undone` variant during the close repaint. Also re-check the Escape ladder below the moved block — `openNoteId`, the three filters, and the planning drawer must still fire in the same order — and re-run both gates (`audit.mjs` and `interaction-check.mjs`; I grepped the behaviour gate and it asserts nothing about the Escape ladder, so it will not catch a regression here — add an assertion for the ordering while you are in it).

standing.element: Notes controls routed through the `ELSEWHERE` table: `[data-act="more"]` ("More actions for this note"), `[data-act="options"]` ("Notes options"), `[data-act="privacy"]`, `[data-act="photo"]` ("Read a photo")
standing.problem: Measured at 1440 in notes.notebook, with and without a note lifted. Pressing each of the four changes nothing on screen: the app's `innerText` is byte-identical before and after, the node count is unchanged, `title` is `null`, `aria-disabled` is `null`, and no popover, strip or tooltip appears. The only answer is a live-region string. "Read a photo" sits beside "Dictate" with an identical computed treatment — background `rgba(0,0,0,0)`, colour `rgba(17,17,17,0.62)`, same border colour, opacity 1, `aria-disabled=null`, `title=null` — and Dictate works, taking the floor to ink. Tasks marks nine equivalent controls `aria-disabled="true"` with a title (List/Schedule/Calendar, Search, More, Settings, both avatars); Notes marks exactly one, the shared dock avatar. Separately, `more`'s sentence — "The rest of Signal Studio is on another screen." — answers a different question than its label asks: the button says "More actions for this note".
standing.consequence: A sighted person presses a live-looking button in the product's own capture row and gets nothing whatsoever. The product reads as broken rather than honest — which is the exact opposite of what the honest-doors decision was for. A screen-reader user is told the control is available, presses it, and is told it lives somewhere else.
standing.fix: Route all four through the treatment Tasks already ships: set `aria-disabled="true"` and the sentence as `title`, and render the sentence in the receipt strip Notes already owns (`.carry`, the one the undo strip uses) so the press produces a visible on-screen answer that decays the same way. Change `more`'s string to name the note's own actions rather than the suite, e.g. "Duplicating, sharing and deleting a note are on another screen. This note is unchanged."
standing.assertion: In every Notes state, every control whose press routes to the `ELSEWHERE` table carries `aria-disabled="true"` and a non-empty `title`, and pressing it makes an element containing that same sentence visible with a non-zero painted box.
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON THE FIX, NOT ON THE PROBLEM — do NOT discard the observation, it reproduces exactly, but this remedy is inert on the very control the finding leads with, names an object Notes does not own, and damages a fifth of its own scope.

WHAT REPRODUCES (chromium, 1440x960, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=notes.notebook`, `src/notes.js:3306` ELSEWHERE):
Every observable claim is exact. With a note lifted onto the desk, pressing each of the four leaves `[data-app="notes"]`.innerText byte-identical and the node count at 254→254; a full-page screenshot before/after pressing `photo` is `Buffer.compare === 0`. `title` is `null` and `aria-disabled` is `null` on all four. `.verb[data-act="photo"]` and `.verb[data-act="voice"]` compute identically — `cursor: pointer`, `color: rgba(17,17,17,0.62)`, `opacity: 1` — and so do their `.dockGlyph` twins; Dictate works, photo does not. `#say` is `class="sr"`, `1x1`, `clip-path: inset(50%)`. And `more`'s mismatch is verbatim: `aria-label="More actions for this note"` answered with "The rest of Signal Studio is on another screen." — the same string `suite-more` uses at `src/notes.js:3110`. That last one alone is misleading.

WHY THE FIX FAILS.

(1) Half (a) is a NO-OP on the control the finding leads with. Notes' only disabled rule is `src/notes.css:1433` — `[data-app="notes"] [aria-disabled="true"] { cursor: default; }`. Tasks' equivalent (`src/tasks.css:1091`) adds `color: var(--ink-3)`. But `--ink-3` is `rgba(17,17,17,0.62)` (`src/notes.css:45`, `src/tasks.css:41`) — which is EXACTLY what `.verb` and `.dockGlyph` already compute. So even porting Tasks' full rule, `photo` next to `voice` would be pixel-identical at rest; the only change is the mouse cursor. Tasks' treatment reads because a disabled `.segItem` (0.62, transparent) sits beside a live one at full ink on a white pill — I measured `segLive` at `rgb(17,17,17)` / `rgb(255,255,255)`. Notes has no such contrast to borrow. The fix does not fix "identical computed treatment", which is the finding's own headline evidence.

(2) `.carry` is not Notes'. It is scoped `[data-app="tasks"] .carry` (`src/tasks.css:1498`, `tasks.js:1002/1018/1040/1055`); `grep carry src/notes.css` returns six prose comments and zero selectors. Notes' strip is `.undo` (`notes.js:1687`, `notes.css:833`) and it is not a receipt strip — `undoStrip()` unconditionally renders an Undo button with a `⌘Z` keycap and a live `for N seconds` countdown driven by `undoTick`. Putting "Reading a photo happens on another screen. Nothing here changes." in it offers to undo a thing that did not happen and starts a 30-second window that does not exist, and it collides with a genuinely pending undo, since `undone` is one slot.

(3) It marks a privacy guarantee as unavailable. `[data-act="privacy"]` (`notes.js:1613`) is not a door — it is the assurance chip, `aria-label="Private to you. Yours until you send something on."` Setting `aria-disabled="true"` on it announces the product's privacy promise as not here yet. That is worse than the defect.

(4) It would open a fourth grammar. I force-pressed the rail's own closed doors on this build: `settings` and Notes' `.dockAvatar` both leave the screenshot byte-identical and answer only in `#say`. The suite's single answer everywhere is aria-disabled + `cursor: default` + `title` + live region. A visible press-receipt in Notes alone re-opens r1's `three-unavailability-grammars`.

TWO EVIDENCE ERRORS. "Tasks marks nine equivalent controls" is inflated. Scoped to `[data-app="tasks"]` at 1440 on tasks.board there are FIVE visible: More, List, Schedule, Calendar, dockAvatar. `.ghost.headSearch` has no box at that width. `Settings` and `.railAvatar` are the SUITE RAIL's — Notes carries both identically; I dumped the document-wide list on notes.notebook and got the same nine, because no product is ever torn down. The real asymmetry is 5 vs 1, not 9 vs 1.
standing.sharpenedFix:
Split the four; they are not one class.

1. `more` — fix the string, which is the misleading half and costs nothing. Give `ELSEWHERE` its own entry instead of borrowing `suite-more`'s: "Duplicating, sharing and deleting a note are on another screen. This note is unchanged." The seat's wording is right; only its delivery was wrong.

2. `photo` and `options` — these are genuinely unavailable. Mark them `aria-disabled="true"` with the sentence as `title` (matching `src/app.js:126` / `src/tasks.js:531`), and add the ONE rule Notes is missing so the mark is visible: `[data-app="notes"] .verb[aria-disabled="true"], [data-app="notes"] .dockGlyph[aria-disabled="true"] { color: var(--ink-4) }` — ink-4 is `rgba(17,17,17,0.30)` and is decorative-only by Notes' own comment at `notes.css:50`, so use `opacity` on the glyph or a dedicated 0.44 step instead if the audit's AA check touches these; that is what must be re-measured. Without a density step the attribute changes nothing but the cursor.

3. `privacy` — leave it live. It is an assurance, not a door. Fix its string only: `fixture.js:617` sets `privacyLong: "Yours until you send something on"` with no terminal stop, so the announcement currently reads "Yours until you send something on Your privacy settings are on another screen." — a run-on. Add the stop at the template, not at the fixture, since the aria-label at `notes.js:1613` already appends its own.

4. If a visible press-receipt is wanted, do it ONCE at suite level, not in Notes. `say()` in `src/app.js` is the single carrier; give it an optional visible twin beside the spine so the rail's `settings`/`me`, Tasks' segItems and Notes' doors all answer the same way. Anything less than that adds a grammar rather than removing one.
standing.breaks:
If shipped as written: adding `aria-disabled="true"` to `photo`/`more`/`options` in Notes produces no visual change (only `cursor: default`), so the panel would read the finding as closed while the defect it names — photo indistinguishable from Dictate — is untouched. Notes' click handler (`notes.js:3090`) has no `[aria-disabled="true"]` guard the way Tasks does (`tasks.js:2415`), so the ELSEWHERE announcement still fires; no functional break there, but the two products would then disagree on whether a disabled control's press is intercepted or handled.

Routing the sentence into the undo strip is the real hazard: `undone` is a single slot and `undoStrip()` always paints Undo + a ticking countdown, so pressing `photo` while a save or a seam-send undo is pending either destroys the pending undo or paints a second strip; `undoTimer`'s expiry path (`notes.js:288`) also moves focus out of the strip if focus is inside it, which would now fire after a press that changed nothing.

Marking `privacy` disabled changes the accessible name of the product's privacy assurance to a dimmed, unavailable control.

RE-MEASURE AFTER IT LANDS: (a) `audit.mjs` AA contrast for any new ink step on `.verb`/`.dockGlyph` against the composited white sheet — 0.30 is well under AA for type and Notes' own comment forbids it as type colour; (b) hit targets on `.dockGlyph` if `cursor`/pointer-events change; (c) `interaction-check.mjs`, specifically the undo assertions, if `.undo` is touched at all; (d) the tab order and focus ring on the four controls, since `aria-disabled` must NOT remove them from the tab order — the whole doctrine at `tasks.js:529` is that a control nobody can reach never gets to say why it is missing; (e) a before/after screenshot diff of `photo` beside `voice` at 1440 and 390 to prove the mark is actually visible, which is the only test that would have caught this fix being inert.

standing.element: `.morePop` (`role="menu"`) and the rail rover — driven at 1440x960
standing.problem: Three separate contract failures on one object. (a) The container is `role="menu"` but its three children are plain `<button aria-disabled="true">` with `role=null` — a menu that reports no menu items. (b) With the menu open and `aria-expanded="true"` on the More tile, ArrowDown/ArrowUp keep walking the rail rover — More → Settings → Avatar — instead of entering the menu; the arrows never reach it. (c) It has no light dismissal: I clicked a card with the menu open and it stayed open; I tabbed through all 20 focus stops of the whole application and it was still open at the end. Only Escape or a second press of More closes it. Tasks' own `.cardMenu` and the Filter/Sort/Display popovers both dismiss correctly on an outside press, via the `toolOpen` branch at the head of `onClick`.
standing.consequence: After one press the menu is stranded open for the rest of the session — three extra focus stops that a keyboard user hits on every pass through the app, invisible to the eye (finding 1), and announced by a screen reader as a menu containing nothing. The contract keys the role advertises do not work.
standing.fix: Give the `.moreItem` buttons `role="menuitem"`; make the rail's arrow rover yield while `[data-rail="plus"]` has `aria-expanded="true"` and route ArrowUp/ArrowDown into `.morePop` instead, wrapping at its ends; and add `.morePop` to the same outside-press dismissal branch the `toolOpen` popovers already use in `onClick`, restoring focus to the More tile when it closes.
standing.assertion: With the More menu open: ArrowDown moves focus to the first `.moreItem`; a press on any element outside `.morePop` and outside the More tile removes `.morePop` from the DOM and returns focus to the More tile; and every element child of `[role="menu"]` has `role="menuitem"`.
standing.verdict:
REFUTED ON PART (c) AND ON THE WHOLE FIX. Parts (a) and (b) are real and reproduce exactly — do NOT discard them — but (c) is the part carrying the severity and the framing ("three separate contract failures", "no light dismissal"), and it is factually wrong about the code, as is every load-bearing premise the proposed fix rests on.

WHAT REPRODUCES. Driven at file://.../_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board, 1440x960.
(a) Exact. `.morePop` is `role="menu"` (line 9300) and its three children are `class="moreItem" aria-disabled="true"` with `role` = null (line 9277). I read it back at runtime: `[{role:null,dis:"true",ti:0}, x3]`. And the suite has its own counter-example 1,500 lines away: `.cardMenu` (line 10802) emits `role="menu"` with `role="menuitem"` on every child and a roving tabindex, and moves focus into the menu on open (line 12452). The rail menu does none of it. That inconsistency is genuine.
(b) Exact. With `aria-expanded="true"` on the More tile, ArrowDown walked plus → settings → me. The rover at line 9666 filters `.rail [data-rail]` by `offsetParent` and never tests `moreOpen`; nothing routes arrows into the panel, and focus is left on the plus tile after open (line 9605).

WHAT DOES NOT. (c) is false as a general claim. The suite ALREADY has the outside-press branch the finding says is missing, and it is sited exactly where the finding asks for one — at the head of `deck`'s click listener, lines 9581-9586: `var insideMore = ...closest(".morePop") || ...closest('[data-rail="plus"]'); if (moreOpen && !insideMore) { moreOpen = false; paintRail(); }`. Driven, it fires and closes the menu on: the ink floor (1430,950), the sheet head (900,40), a `.tick`, any of the four `[data-act="tool"]` buttons, a Notes `.idxRow`, and a Timeline `.b-grab`. One gesture out of seven fails — the Tasks card body, which is the one the seat used — and it fails for a reason the finding never names. The card opens on **pointerup** (line 13271), which calls `mount()` and re-renders the board before the click is dispatched; the click target is detached, so no click event reaches `deck` at all. I instrumented both `deck` and `document` in the bubble phase and the log after a card press was empty: `[]`. This is a propagation hole in one control, not a missing dismissal model.

WHY THE FIX IS WRONG — three ways, and the first two are checkable facts.
1. "Tasks' own `.cardMenu` ... dismiss[es] correctly ... via the `toolOpen` branch at the head of `onClick`" is false. `.cardMenu` does not touch `toolOpen`. It ships a dedicated full-screen overlay, `<div class="menuVeil" data-act="closemenu">` (line 10801, CSS line 1780, handled at 12514), which is why Playwright reported "menuVeil intercepts pointer events" when I tried to click past it.
2. "the Filter/Sort/Display popovers ... dismiss correctly on an outside press" is false on the seat's own repro. I opened Filter and clicked a card: `{tool:true}` — still open. The `toolOpen` branch at line 12139 has the identical hole for the identical reason. So the proposed remedy is "copy the branch that fails on exactly the gesture you used to prove the bug." It would not close `.morePop` on a card press.
3. Wrong layer. `onClick` is bound to Tasks' `host` (line 13314). The rail is the shell's, rendered once by `railHtml`/`paintRail` for all three products. Wiring rail dismissal into Tasks' handler duplicates a shell branch that already exists and silently drops it in Notes and Timeline — where it currently works.

SEVERITY. The seat's class rested on (c). What survives is a defect, not blocking or misleading: every door in the panel is reachable by Tab (I walked it: plus → All projects → Inbox → Help → the sheet), named, and speaks its "Not here yet" sentence; Escape closes and restores focus (line 9648); six of seven outside presses close it. Nothing the product says to a person is untrue. It sits at the defect/misleading line only because `role="menu"` with zero menuitems is a false assertion to AT — I do not class it misleading because that is the half of the finding the seat argued least. Nothing here is asserted by `interaction-check.mjs`; I checked — it has no `morePop`/`moreOpen` assertion.
standing.sharpenedFix:
Fix the two real halves, in the shell, and fix the propagation hole once for all four surfaces instead of copying a broken branch.

1. ARIA and keyboard, together — they are one change, not two. At line 9277 add `role="menuitem"` and `tabindex="-1"` to each `.moreItem`; keep `aria-disabled="true"` and the title. In the `plus` branch at line 9604, focus the first `.moreItem` instead of the plus tile on open (mirroring `.cardMenu` at line 12452), and keep focusing the plus tile on close. In the keydown handler at line 9666, before the `var tile = ...` test, add a branch: if `moreOpen` and `event.target.closest(".morePop")`, ArrowDown/ArrowUp (ArrowRight/ArrowLeft at <=720, matching the `horizontal` predicate already computed at line 9679) move the roving stop within `[].slice.call(deck.querySelectorAll(".moreItem"))` with wrap, Home/End go to the ends, and `preventDefault` + `stopPropagation` as the rover already does. The rail rover then needs no "yield" clause — focus is inside `.morePop`, not on a `[data-rail]`, so it never matches. Once items are roving `tabindex="-1"`, add focusout dismissal: on `deck` focusout, if `moreOpen` and neither `event.target` nor `relatedTarget` is inside `.morePop` or on the plus tile, close and repaint — that is what makes the seat's "still open after 20 tab stops" observation correct behaviour rather than a bug, and it is only correct once the panel is a single tab stop.
2. Light dismissal — move the existing branch, do not duplicate it. Change lines 9581-9586 from a `click` listener to a `pointerdown` listener on `deck` (keep the `insideMore` test verbatim; add `.railAdd`? no — leave the predicate alone). I verified this works: with More open, a card press produced `["deck-pd:cardNote"]` on `deck`, i.e. pointerdown reaches the shell before `mount()` at line 13271 detaches the target. That is the only gesture currently failing, and this closes it without touching Tasks.
3. Optional, separately scoped: the same pointerdown move fixes `toolOpen` at line 12139, which I measured failing on the same gesture. File it as its own finding — do not bundle it here.

RE-MEASURE AFTER IT LANDS. (i) `interaction-check.mjs` and `audit.mjs` both green — the focus audit at interaction-check.mjs:80 counts focus stops, and roving `tabindex="-1"` removes three; confirm it still passes (it should: the invisible-focusable test only trips on focusable AND invisible, and these are visible). (ii) The honest-doors constraint says All projects, Inbox and Help are "in the tab order". Under a roving menu they are reachable through the More tile, which is itself a tab stop, but they are no longer three independent Tab stops — get the founder's read on that before shipping, because it is the one place this fix touches a non-negotiable. (iii) At <=720 the panel carries a fourth item (Settings joins it, line 9573) and the arrows lie down; re-drive at 390. (iv) Moving dismissal to pointerdown means a press that BEGINS on the floor and ends on the plus tile now closes then reopens — check the plus tile's own toggle at line 9600 does not double-fire, and re-drive "press plus, press plus again" and "press plus, drag a card". (v) Escape from inside the panel (line 9648) and `paintRail`'s focus restore (line 9614) both still land on the plus tile.
standing.breaks: The roving-tabindex change removes three independent Tab stops (All projects, Inbox, Help), which brushes the "honest doors are in the tab order" constraint — that is the one thing here needing a founder decision rather than an engineering call, and it is why this fix cannot be shipped blind. Moving the shell's dismissal from `click` to `pointerdown` changes when the panel closes relative to a drag: a press that begins on the floor now closes the panel before any drag starts, which is correct but changes the plus tile's toggle timing, so "press plus twice" and "press plus then drag a card" both need re-driving. Focusing the first `.moreItem` on open changes what a screen reader announces at open — re-listen to the `say("More, open.")` line at 9607, which currently speaks while focus is still on the tile. Re-measure: both gates green; the focus-stop count in interaction-check.mjs:80; the panel at 390x844 where it carries a fourth item and horizontal arrows; Escape and `paintRail` focus restore; and the `.morePop` dismissal on all seven gestures I drove (floor, sheet head, tick, tool button, card body, Notes `.idxRow`, Timeline `.b-grab`).

standing.element: `.viewTools .ghost` ("Filter") and its `.toolDot` badge, with any filter active
standing.problem: Pressing "1 overdue" raises a count badge on the Filter button. Measured at 1280: the badge box is x 1058–1072, y 184–198; the label span is x 1034–1063, y 189–206. They intersect by 5px horizontally and 9px vertically, so the badge sits on the final "r" and the control reads "Filte¹". Identical 5x9 overlap at 768, 1280, 1440 and 1920, and in both variants — the button is a fixed 73px wide, so the badge has nowhere to go. The badge also carries `aria-hidden="true"` and the button has no `aria-label`, so the count exists only in paint.
standing.consequence: The one control that explains why the board just went from thirteen cards to one renders with its last letter obscured, in a screenshot-quality surface. A screen-reader user hears "Filter" whether one filter is applied or none, and has nothing in the accessible name to tell them the board is being filtered.
standing.fix: Inset `.toolDot` into the button's padding box so its left edge begins at least 4px after the label span's right edge, letting the button grow rather than overlap — the same relationship the head's `1 today` / `1 overdue` chips already hold between number and word. Set the button's `aria-label` from the same accessor that renders the dot: "Filter, 1 applied" when the count is non-zero, "Filter" otherwise.
standing.assertion: At 768/1280/1440/1920 in both variants, with a filter active, the `.toolDot` and label-span bounding boxes do not intersect, and the Filter button's accessible name contains the active-filter count.
standing.verdict: REFUTED ON THE FIX, NOT ON THE PROBLEM — the occlusion is real, reproduces to the tenth of a pixel, and must NOT be discarded. But the remedy as written cannot produce the effect it claims, one of its structural facts is false, and the accessibility half rests on a claim that driving disproves. WHAT REPRODUCES (chromium, `_gate-suite.html?v=paper&state=tasks.board`, pressing the "1 overdue" chip) The geometry is exact. At 1280: badge x 1058.4–1072.4, y 183.8–197.8; label span x 1034.0–1063.4, y 189.3–206.3. Overlap 5.0px horizontal, 8.5px vertical. Identical at 768, 1440, 1920, and byte-identical in `v=ink`. It is worse than the seat says: I took per-character Range rects and the final "r" advance box is 1058.6–1063.4 — the badge's left edge lands 0.2px BEFORE the "r" begins and covers its entire advance. At deviceScaleFactor 10 the r's shoulder and terminal are gone and only a bare stem survives, so the control reads "Filte|". On the flagship view's primary control, that is a real defect.
